chapters: And He called Moshe, and Havayah spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, and say to them: A man when he brings from you an offering to Havayah, from the animal, from the cattle and from the flock you shall bring your offering.
If a burnt offering is his offering from the cattle, he shall bring an unblemished male; to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he shall bring it, for his acceptance before Havayah.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him to atone for him.

And he shall slaughter the young bull before Havayah, and the sons of Aharon, the priests, shall bring the blood, and they shall cast the blood upon the altar around, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And he shall flay the burnt offering, and cut it into its pieces.
And the sons of Aharon the priest shall put fire upon the altar, and arrange wood upon the fire.
And the sons of Aharon, the priests, shall arrange the pieces, the head and the fat, upon the wood that is upon the fire that is upon the altar.
And its innards and its legs he shall wash in water, and the priest shall burn the whole upon the altar, a burnt offering, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And if his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall bring an unblemished male.
And he shall slaughter it upon the side of the altar northward before Havayah, and the sons of Aharon, the priests, shall cast its blood upon the altar around.
And he shall cut it into its pieces, and its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them upon the wood that is upon the fire that is upon the altar.
And the innards and the legs he shall wash in water, and the priest shall bring the whole, and burn it upon the altar; a burnt offering it is, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And if his offering to Havayah is a burnt offering from the bird, and he shall bring from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons his offering.
And the priest shall bring it to the altar, and pinch off its head, and burn it upon the altar, and its blood shall be squeezed upon the wall of the altar.
And he shall remove its crop with its feathers, and cast it beside the altar eastward, to the place of the ashes.

And he shall split it by its wings, he shall not separate, and the priest shall burn it upon the altar, upon the wood that is upon the fire; a burnt offering it is, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And a soul when it brings an offering of a meal offering to Havayah, fine flour shall be his offering, and he shall pour upon it oil, and put upon it frankincense.

And he shall bring it to the sons of Aharon, the priests, and he shall take from there a full handful of its fine flour and of its oil, upon all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its memorial portion upon the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And the remainder from the meal offering shall be for Aharon and for his sons, a holy of holies from the fire offerings of Havayah.
And when you bring an offering of a meal offering baked in an oven, fine flour, unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil.
And if a meal offering upon the pan is your offering, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Break it into pieces, and pour upon it oil; a meal offering it is.
And if a meal offering of a deep pan is your offering, fine flour with oil shall be made.
And you shall bring the meal offering that is made from these to Havayah, and he shall bring it to the priest, and he shall bring it near to the altar.
And the priest shall lift from the meal offering its memorial portion, and burn it upon the altar, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And the remainder from the meal offering shall be for Aharon and for his sons, a holy of holies from the fire offerings of Havayah.
Every meal offering that you bring to Havayah shall not be made leavened, for all leaven and all honey you shall not burn from it a fire offering to Havayah.
You shall bring them to Havayah as an offering of first fruits, and to the altar they shall not ascend for a pleasing aroma.

And every offering of your meal offering with salt you shall salt, and you shall not withhold the salt of the covenant of your Elokim from upon your meal offering; upon every offering of yours you shall bring salt.
And if you bring a meal offering of first fruits to Havayah, fresh grain roasted in fire, ground from soft kernels, you shall bring the meal offering of your first fruits.
And you shall give upon it oil, and put upon it frankincense; a meal offering it is.
And the priest shall burn its memorial portion, from its ground grain and from its oil, upon all its frankincense, a fire offering to Havayah.
And if a peace offering is his offering, if he brings it from the cattle, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished before Havayah.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of his offering, and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and the sons of Aharon, the priests, shall cast the blood upon the altar around.
And he shall bring from the peace offering a fire offering to Havayah, the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is upon the innards.
And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that is upon the flanks, and the diaphragm upon the liver, he shall remove it with the kidneys.
And the sons of Aharon shall burn them upon the altar, upon the burnt offering that is upon the wood that is upon the fire, a fire offering of a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And if his offering for a peace offering to Havayah is from the flock, whether male or female, he shall bring it unblemished.
If a lamb he brings as his offering, and he shall bring it before Havayah.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of his offering, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and the sons of Aharon shall cast its blood upon the altar around.

And he shall bring from the peace offering a fire offering to Havayah: its fat, the whole fat tail, he shall remove opposite the spine, and the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is upon the innards.
And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that is upon the flanks, and the diaphragm upon the liver, he shall remove it with the kidneys.
And the priest shall burn it upon the altar, food of a fire offering to Havayah.
And if a goat is his offering, and he shall bring it before Havayah.
And he shall lean his hand upon its head, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and the sons of Aharon shall cast its blood upon the altar around.
And he shall bring from it his offering, a fire offering to Havayah, the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is upon the innards.
And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that is upon the flanks, and the diaphragm upon the liver, he shall remove it with the kidneys.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, food of a fire offering for a pleasing aroma; all fat is for Havayah.
An eternal statute for your generations, in all your dwellings: all fat and all blood you shall not eat.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, saying: A soul when it sins unwittingly from all the commandments of Havayah that shall not be done, and does from one of them.
If the anointed priest sins to the guilt of the people, and he shall bring for his sin that he sinned an unblemished young bull to Havayah for a sin offering.
And he shall bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before Havayah, and lean his hand upon the head of the bull, and slaughter the bull before Havayah.
And the anointed priest shall take from the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle from the blood seven times before Havayah, before the face of the Curtain of the Sanctuary.

And the priest shall put from the blood upon the horns of the altar of the incense of spices before Havayah, which is in the Tent of Meeting, and all the blood of the bull he shall pour at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And all the fat of the bull of the sin offering he shall lift from it: the fat that covers upon the innards, and all the fat that is upon the innards.
And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that is upon the flanks, and the diaphragm upon the liver, he shall remove it with the kidneys.
As it is lifted from the ox of the peace offering, and the priest shall burn them upon the altar of the burnt offering.
And the hide of the bull, and all its flesh, with its head, and with its legs, and its innards, and its dung.
And he shall take out the whole bull to outside the camp, to a pure place, to the pouring place of the ashes, and burn it upon wood in fire; upon the pouring place of the ashes it shall be burned.
And if the whole congregation of Yisroel errs, and a matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do one from all the commandments of Havayah that shall not be done, and they are guilty.
And the sin that they sinned upon it is known, and the assembly shall bring a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
And the elders of the congregation shall lean their hands upon the head of the bull before Havayah, and he shall slaughter the bull before Havayah.
And the anointed priest shall bring from the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting.
And the priest shall dip his finger from the blood, and sprinkle seven times before Havayah, before the face of the Curtain.

And from the blood he shall put upon the horns of the altar that is before Havayah, that is in the Tent of Meeting, and all the blood he shall pour at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And all its fat he shall lift from it, and burn it upon the altar.
And he shall do to the bull as he did to the bull of the sin offering, so he shall do to it, and the priest shall atone for them, and it shall be forgiven them.
And he shall take out the bull to outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull; a sin offering of the assembly it is.
When a ruler sins, and does one from all the commandments of Havayah his Elokim that shall not be done, unwittingly, and is guilty.
Or his sin that he sinned in it is made known to him, and he shall bring his offering, an unblemished male goat.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of the goat, and slaughter it in the place where he slaughters the burnt offering before Havayah; a sin offering it is.

And the priest shall take from the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and its blood he shall pour at the base of the altar of the burnt offering.
And all its fat he shall burn upon the altar, like the fat of the peace offering, and the priest shall atone for him from his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
And if one soul sins unwittingly from the people of the land, in doing one of the commandments of Havayah that shall not be done, and is guilty.
Or his sin that he sinned is made known to him, and he shall bring his offering, an unblemished female goat, for his sin that he sinned.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of the sin offering, and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.
And the priest shall take from its blood with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and all its blood he shall pour at the base of the altar.

And all its fat he shall remove, as was removed the fat from the peace offering, and the priest shall burn it upon the altar for a pleasing aroma to Havayah, and the priest shall atone for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
And if a lamb he brings as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring an unblemished female.
And he shall lean his hand upon the head of the sin offering, and slaughter it for a sin offering in the place where he slaughters the burnt offering.
And the priest shall take from the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and all its blood he shall pour at the base of the altar.

And all its fat he shall remove, as is removed the fat of the lamb from the peace offering, and the priest shall burn them upon the altar, upon the fire offerings of Havayah, and the priest shall atone for him for his sin that he sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.
And a soul when it sins, and hears the voice of an oath, and he is a witness, either he saw or he knew, if he does not tell, and he shall bear his iniquity.

Or a soul that touches any impure thing, or the carcass of an impure wild beast, or the carcass of an impure animal, or the carcass of an impure swarming creature, and it is hidden from him, and he is impure, and he is guilty.
Or when he touches the impurity of man, to all his impurity that he becomes impure by it, and it is hidden from him, and he knew, and he is guilty.
Or a soul when it swears to utter with lips to do evil or to do good, to all that a man utters in an oath, and it is hidden from him, and he knew, and he is guilty of one of these.
And it shall be when he is guilty of one of these, and he shall confess that he sinned upon it.
And he shall bring his guilt offering to Havayah for his sin that he sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a female goat, for a sin offering, and the priest shall atone for him from his sin.

And if his hand does not reach enough for a lamb, and he shall bring his guilt offering that he sinned, two turtledoves or two young pigeons to Havayah, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
And he shall bring them to the priest, and he shall bring that which is for the sin offering first, and pinch off its head opposite its nape, and he shall not separate.
And he shall sprinkle from the blood of the sin offering upon the wall of the altar, and the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed to the base of the altar; a sin offering it is.
And the second he shall make a burnt offering according to the law, and the priest shall atone for him from his sin that he sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.

And if his hand does not reach to two turtledoves or to two young pigeons, and he shall bring his offering that he sinned, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall not put upon it oil, and he shall not give upon it frankincense, for a sin offering it is.
And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take from it a full handful, its memorial portion, and burn it upon the altar, upon the fire offerings of Havayah; a sin offering it is.
And the priest shall atone for him for his sin that he sinned from one of these, and it shall be forgiven him; and it shall be for the priest like the meal offering.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

A soul when it commits a trespass, and sins unwittingly from the sacred things of Havayah, and he shall bring his guilt offering to Havayah, an unblemished ram from the flock, by your valuation of silver shekels, by the shekel of the Sanctuary, for a guilt offering.

And that which he sinned from the sacred thing he shall pay, and its fifth he shall add upon it, and give it to the priest, and the priest shall atone for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.
And if a soul sins, and does one from all the commandments of Havayah that shall not be done, and he did not know, and he is guilty, and he shall bear his iniquity.

And he shall bring an unblemished ram from the flock, by your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest, and the priest shall atone for him for his unwitting sin that he sinned unwittingly, and he did not know, and it shall be forgiven him.
A guilt offering it is; he has surely been guilty before Havayah.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
A soul when it sins, and commits a trespass against Havayah, and lies to his fellow about a deposit, or about a loan, or about robbery, or oppressed his fellow.
Or found a lost item, and lied about it, and swore falsely, about one from all that a man does to sin in them.

And it shall be when he sins and is guilty, and he shall return the robbery that he robbed, or the oppression that he oppressed, or the deposit that was deposited with him, or the lost item that he found.
Or from all that he swore upon it falsely, and he shall pay it in its principal, and its fifth he shall add upon it; to him whose it is he shall give it on the day of his guilt.
And his guilt offering he shall bring to Havayah, an unblemished ram from the flock, by your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest.
And the priest shall atone for him before Havayah, and it shall be forgiven him, for one from all that he does to be guilty in it.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

Command Aharon and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt offering: it is the burnt offering upon its pyre upon the altar all the night until the morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning in it.

And the priest shall put on his linen tunic, and linen trousers he shall put on upon his flesh, and he shall lift the ashes that the fire consumes of the burnt offering upon the altar, and put it beside the altar.
And he shall take off his garments, and put on other garments, and take out the ashes to outside the camp, to a pure place.

And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning in it, it shall not be extinguished, and the priest shall kindle wood upon it in the morning, in the morning, and arrange upon it the burnt offering, and burn upon it the fats of the peace offerings.
A perpetual fire shall be kept burning upon the altar, it shall not be extinguished.
And this is the law of the meal offering: the sons of Aharon shall bring it near before Havayah, to the face of the altar.

And he shall lift from it with his handful, from the fine flour of the meal offering and from its oil, and all the frankincense that is upon the meal offering, and burn it upon the altar, a pleasing aroma, its memorial portion to Havayah.
And Aharon and his sons shall eat the remainder of it; unleavened it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it.
It shall not be baked leavened; I have given it to them as their portion from My fire offerings; a holy of holies it is, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.
Every male among the children of Aharon shall eat it, an eternal statute for your generations, from the fire offerings of Havayah; all that touches them shall become holy.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

This is the offering of Aharon and his sons that they shall bring to Havayah on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, a perpetual meal offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
Upon a pan with oil it shall be made, you shall bring it fried; you shall bring baked pieces of a meal offering, a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And the priest who is anointed in his stead from among his sons shall make it; an eternal statute to Havayah, wholly it shall be burned.
And every meal offering of a priest shall be wholly burned; it shall not be eaten.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before Havayah; a holy of holies it is.
The priest who offers it as a sin offering shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
All that touches its flesh shall become holy, and whatever is sprinkled of its blood upon a garment, you shall wash that which was sprinkled upon it in a holy place.
And an earthenware vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken, and if in a bronze vessel it was cooked, it shall be scoured and rinsed in water.
Every male among the priests shall eat it; a holy of holies it is.
And every sin offering from which its blood is brought to the Tent of Meeting to atone in the holy place shall not be eaten; in fire it shall be burned.
And this is the law of the guilt offering; a holy of holies it is.
In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall slaughter the guilt offering, and its blood he shall cast upon the altar around.
And all its fat he shall bring from it: the tail, and the fat that covers the innards.
And the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, that is upon the flanks, and the diaphragm upon the liver, he shall remove it with the kidneys.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, a fire offering to Havayah; a guilt offering it is.
Every male among the priests shall eat it; in a holy place it shall be eaten; a holy of holies it is.
As the sin offering, so the guilt offering, one law is theirs; the priest who atones with it, his it shall be.
And the priest who brings the burnt offering of a man, the hide of the burnt offering that he brought shall be for the priest.
And every meal offering that is baked in the oven, and all that is made in a deep pan and upon a pan, it shall be for the priest who brings it.
And every meal offering mixed with oil and dry, it shall be for all the sons of Aharon, one like another.
And this is the law of the peace offering that he brings to Havayah.
If for thanksgiving he brings it, and he shall bring upon the thanks offering unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and fine flour boiled, loaves mixed with oil.
Upon loaves of leavened bread he shall bring his offering, upon the thanks offering of his peace offerings.
And he shall bring from it one from each offering, a gift to Havayah; it shall be for the priest who casts the blood of the peace offerings.
And the flesh of the thanks offering of his peace offerings, on the day of his offering it shall be eaten; he shall not leave from it until morning.
And if a vow or a freewill offering is the offering of his offering, on the day he brings his offering it shall be eaten, and on the morrow, and the remainder of it shall be eaten.
And the remainder from the flesh of the offering, on the third day it shall be burned in fire.

And if any of the flesh of his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it shall not be accepted; it shall not be reckoned to him who brings it; a detestable thing it shall be, and the soul that eats from it shall bear its iniquity.
And the flesh that touches any impure thing shall not be eaten; in fire it shall be burned; and the flesh, every pure person shall eat flesh.
And the soul that eats flesh from the peace offering that is for Havayah, and his impurity is upon him, and that soul shall be cut off from its people.

And a soul when it touches any impure thing, in the impurity of man, or in an impure animal, or in any impure detestable thing, and eats from the flesh of the peace offering that is for Havayah, and that soul shall be cut off from its people.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, saying: All fat of ox and sheep and goat you shall not eat.
And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a mauled animal shall be made for all work, and you shall not eat it at all.
For anyone who eats fat from the animal that one offers from it a fire offering to Havayah, and the soul that eats shall be cut off from its people.
And all blood you shall not eat, in all your dwellings, of birds and of animals.
Every soul that eats any blood, and that soul shall be cut off from its people.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, saying: He who brings his peace offering to Havayah, he shall bring his offering to Havayah from his peace offering.
His hands shall bring the fire offerings of Havayah; he shall bring the fat upon the breast, the breast, to wave it as a wave offering before Havayah.
And the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar, and the breast shall be for Aharon and for his sons.
And the right thigh you shall give as a gift to the priest, from your peace offerings.
He who brings the blood of the peace offerings and the fat, from the sons of Aharon, the right thigh shall be his for a portion.

For the breast of the waving and the thigh of the gift I have taken from the children of Yisroel, from their peace offerings, and I give them to Aharon the priest and to his sons, for an eternal statute from the children of Yisroel.
This is the anointing portion of Aharon and the anointing portion of his sons, from the fire offerings of Havayah, on the day He brought them near to serve as priests to Havayah.
That Havayah commanded to give to them on the day He anointed them, from the children of Yisroel, an eternal statute for their generations.
This is the law for the burnt offering, for the meal offering, and for the sin offering, and for the guilt offering, and for the investiture offerings, and for the peace offering.
That Havayah commanded Moshe on Mount Sinai, on the day He commanded the children of Yisroel to bring their offerings to Havayah, in the wilderness of Sinai.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Take Aharon and his sons with him, and the vestments, and the anointing oil, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And gather the whole congregation to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And Moshe did as Havayah commanded him, and the congregation was gathered to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And Moshe said to the congregation: This is the thing that Havayah commanded to do.
And Moshe brought Aharon and his sons near, and washed them in water.
And he put upon him the tunic, and girded him with the belt, and clothed him with the robe, and put upon him the ephod, and girded him with the belt of the ephod, and adorned him with it.
And he put upon him the breastpiece, and put into the breastpiece the Urim and the Tumim.
And he put the mitre upon his head, and put upon the mitre, toward his face, the golden frontplate, the sacred diadem, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And Moshe took the anointing oil, and anointed the Mishkan and all that was in it, and consecrated them.
And he sprinkled from it upon the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base, to consecrate them.
And he poured from the anointing oil upon the head of Aharon, and anointed him to consecrate him.
And Moshe brought the sons of Aharon near, and clothed them in tunics, and girded them with a belt, and he wrapped headdresses around them, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And he brought near the bull of the sin offering, and Aharon and his sons leaned their hands upon the head of the bull of the sin offering.

And he slaughtered, and Moshe took the blood, and put it upon the horns of the altar around with his finger, and purified the altar, and the blood he poured at the base of the altar, and consecrated it to atone for it.
And he took all the fat that is upon the innards, and the diaphragm of the liver, and the two kidneys and their fat, and Moshe burned them upon the altar.
And the bull, and its hide, and its flesh, and its dung, he burned in fire outside the camp, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And he brought near the ram of the burnt offering, and Aharon and his sons leaned their hands upon the head of the ram.
And he slaughtered, and Moshe cast the blood upon the altar around.
And the ram he cut into its pieces, and Moshe burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat.

And the innards and the legs he washed in water, and Moshe burned the whole ram upon the altar; a burnt offering it is for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering it is to Havayah, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And he brought near the second ram, the ram of investiture, and Aharon and his sons leaned their hands upon the head of the ram.
And he slaughtered, and Moshe took from its blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aharon, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot.

And he brought near the sons of Aharon, and Moshe put from the blood upon the tip of their right ear, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the big toe of their right foot, and Moshe cast the blood upon the altar around.
And he took the fat, and the tail, and all the fat that is upon the innards, and the diaphragm of the liver, and the two kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh.
And from the basket of unleavened bread that is before Havayah he took one unleavened loaf, and one loaf of oil bread, and one wafer, and put them upon the fats and upon the right thigh.
And he put the whole upon the palms of Aharon and upon the palms of his sons, and waved them as a wave offering before Havayah.
And Moshe took them from upon their palms, and burned them upon the altar, upon the burnt offering; investiture offerings they are for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering it is to Havayah.
And Moshe took the breast, and waved it as a wave offering before Havayah; from the ram of investiture, for Moshe it was for a portion, as Havayah commanded Moshe.

And Moshe took from the anointing oil and from the blood that is upon the altar, and sprinkled upon Aharon, upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him, and consecrated Aharon, his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.

And Moshe said to Aharon and to his sons: Cook the flesh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and there eat it and the bread that is in the basket of investiture, as I commanded, saying: Aharon and his sons shall eat it.
And the remainder of the flesh and of the bread, in fire you shall burn.
And from the entrance of the Tent of Meeting you shall not go out seven days, until the day of completion of the days of your investiture, for seven days He shall fill your hand.
As was done on this day, Havayah commanded to do, to atone for you.
And at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting you shall dwell day and night seven days, and keep the charge of Havayah, and you shall not die, for so I was commanded.
And Aharon and his sons did all the things that Havayah commanded by the hand of Moshe.
And it was on the eighth day, Moshe called Aharon and his sons and the elders of Yisroel.
And he said to Aharon: Take for yourself an unblemished young calf for a sin offering and an unblemished ram for a burnt offering, and bring them near before Havayah.
And to the children of Yisroel speak, saying: Take a goat for a sin offering, and an unblemished year-old calf and lamb for a burnt offering.
And a bull and a ram for peace offerings, to slaughter before Havayah, and a meal offering mixed with oil, for today Havayah appears to you.
And they took what Moshe commanded, to the face of the Tent of Meeting, and came near all the congregation, and stood before Havayah.
And Moshe said: This is the thing that Havayah commanded you shall do, and the glory of Havayah shall appear to you.

And Moshe said to Aharon: Come near to the altar, and do your sin offering and your burnt offering, and atone for yourself and for the people, and do the offering of the people and atone for them, as Havayah commanded.
And Aharon came near to the altar, and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was his.
And the sons of Aharon brought the blood near to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood, and put it upon the horns of the altar, and the blood he poured at the base of the altar.
And the fat, and the kidneys, and the diaphragm from the liver, from the sin offering, he burned upon the altar, as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And the flesh and the hide he burned in fire outside the camp.
And he slaughtered the burnt offering, and the sons of Aharon brought the blood near to him, and he cast it upon the altar around.
And the burnt offering they brought near to him in its pieces, and the head, and he burned it upon the altar.
And he washed the innards and the legs, and burned them upon the burnt offering, upon the altar.
And he brought near the offering of the people, and took the goat of the sin offering that was for the people, and slaughtered it, and offered it as a sin offering like the first.
And he brought near the burnt offering, and did it according to the law.
And he brought near the meal offering, and filled his palm from it, and burned it upon the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning.
And he slaughtered the bull and the ram, the peace offering that was for the people, and the sons of Aharon brought the blood near to him, and he cast it upon the altar around.
And the fats from the bull, and from the ram, the tail, and the covering, and the kidneys, and the diaphragm of the liver.
And they placed the fats upon the breasts, and he burned the fats upon the altar.
And Aharon waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before Havayah, as Moshe commanded.
And Aharon lifted his hands toward the people, and blessed them, and came down from doing the sin offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
And Moshe and Aharon came to the Tent of Meeting, and they went out, and blessed the people, and the glory of Havayah appeared to all the people.
And fire came out from before Havayah, and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering and the fats, and all the people saw, and they sang out, and fell upon their faces.
And the sons of Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, took, each his fire pan, and put in them fire, and put upon it incense, and brought near before Havayah a strange fire, that He had not commanded them.
And fire came out from before Havayah, and consumed them, and they died before Havayah.
And Moshe said to Aharon: It is that which Havayah spoke, saying: Through those near to Me I shall be sanctified, and before all the people I shall be glorified; and Aharon was silent.
And Moshe called Mishael and Eltzafan, sons of Uziel, uncle of Aharon, and said to them: Come near, carry your brethren from before the Sanctuary to outside the camp.
And they came near, and carried them in their tunics to outside the camp, as Moshe spoke.

And Moshe said to Aharon, and to Elazar and to Itamar his sons: Your heads you shall not let grow wild, and your garments you shall not tear, and you shall not die, and upon all the congregation He shall be angry; and your brethren, all the house of Yisroel, shall weep for the burning that Havayah burned.
And from the entrance of the Tent of Meeting you shall not go out, lest you die, for the anointing oil of Havayah is upon you; and they did as the word of Moshe.
And Havayah spoke to Aharon, saying:
Wine and strong drink you shall not drink, you and your sons with you, when you come to the Tent of Meeting, and you shall not die; an eternal statute for your generations.
And to distinguish between the sacred and between the profane, and between the impure and between the pure.
And to teach the children of Yisroel all the statutes that Havayah spoke to them by the hand of Moshe.

And Moshe spoke to Aharon, and to Elazar and to Itamar his sons, the remaining: Take the meal offering that remains from the fire offerings of Havayah, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for a holy of holies it is.
And you shall eat it in a holy place, for your portion and the portion of your sons it is, from the fire offerings of Havayah, for so I was commanded.

And the breast of the waving and the thigh of the lifting you shall eat in a pure place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for your portion and the portion of your sons they are given, from the peace offerings of the children of Yisroel.

The thigh of the lifting and the breast of the waving, upon the fire offerings of the fats they shall bring, to wave them as a wave offering before Havayah, and it shall be for you and for your sons with you, for an eternal statute, as Havayah commanded.
And Moshe inquired about the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it was burned; and he was angry upon Elazar and upon Itamar, sons of Aharon, the remaining, saying:
Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place, for a holy of holies it is, and He gave it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to atone for them before Havayah?
Behold, its blood was not brought to the Sanctuary within; eating you shall eat it in the holy place, as I commanded.

And Aharon spoke to Moshe: Behold, today they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before Havayah, and such as these befell me, and I ate a sin offering today, would it be good in the eyes of Havayah?
And Moshe heard, and it was good in his eyes.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying to them:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, saying: This is the living creature that you may eat, from all the animals that are upon the earth.
Every one that divides the hoof, and splits the cleft of the hooves, bringing up the cud, among the animals, you shall eat it.
But this you shall not eat, from those that bring up the cud and from those that divide the hoof: the camel, for it brings up the cud, but it does not divide a hoof; impure it is to you.
And the hyrax, for it brings up the cud, but it does not divide a hoof; impure it is to you.
And the hare, for it brings up the cud, but it has not divided a hoof; impure it is to you.
And the pig, for it divides the hoof, and splits the cleft of the hoof, but it does not chew the cud; impure it is to you.
From their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; impure they are to you.
This you shall eat, from all that is in the water: all that has a fin and a scale in the water, in the seas and in the rivers, them you shall eat.

And all that does not have a fin and a scale, in the seas and in the rivers, from all the swarming creatures of the water and from all the living soul that is in the water, a detestable thing they are to you.
And a detestable thing they shall be to you; from their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall detest.
All that does not have a fin and a scale in the water, a detestable thing it is to you.
And these you shall detest from the birds; they shall not be eaten, a detestable thing they are: the griffon vulture, and the bearded vulture, and the lappet-faced vulture.
And the kite, and the buzzard after its kind.
Every raven after its kind.
And the ostrich, and the swift, and the seagull, and the sparrow hawk after its kind.
And the little owl, and the fish owl, and the short-eared owl.
And the barn owl, and the eagle-owl, and the roller.
And the stork, the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every swarming creature of the bird that walks upon four, a detestable thing it is to you.
But this you shall eat, from all the swarming creatures of the bird that walk upon four, that has legs above its feet, to leap with them upon the earth.
These of them you shall eat: the locust after its kind, and the bald locust after its kind, and the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.
And every swarming creature of the bird that has four feet, a detestable thing it is to you.
And by these you shall become impure; all who touch their carcasses shall be impure until the evening.
And all who carry from their carcasses shall wash his garments, and be impure until the evening.
For every animal that divides the hoof, but it does not split a cleft, and it does not bring up cud, impure they are to you; all who touch them shall be impure.
And all that walks upon its paws, among all the living creatures that walk upon four, impure they are to you; all who touch their carcasses shall be impure until the evening.
And he who carries their carcasses shall wash his garments, and be impure until the evening; impure they are to you.
And this is impure to you among the swarming creatures that swarm upon the earth: the marten, and the mouse, and the spiny-tailed lizard after its kind.
And the shrew, and the monitor, and the lizard, and the skink, and the chameleon.
These are the impure ones to you among all the swarming creatures; all who touch them in their death shall be impure until the evening.

And all upon which any of them falls in their death shall be impure, from any wooden vessel, or garment, or leather, or sack, any vessel with which work is done, in water it shall be brought, and it shall be impure until the evening, and it shall be pure.
And every earthenware vessel into which falls from them into it, all that is in it shall be impure, and it you shall break.
All the food that is eaten, upon which water comes, shall be impure, and every drink that is drunk in any vessel shall be impure.
And all upon which any of their carcasses falls shall be impure; oven and stove shall be broken; impure they are, and impure they shall be to you.
But a spring and a cistern, a gathering of water, shall be pure; and one who touches their carcasses shall be impure.
And when any of their carcasses falls upon any sown seed, pure it is.
And when water is put upon seed, and any of their carcasses falls upon it, impure it is to you.
And when any animal that is for you to eat dies, one who touches its carcass shall be impure until the evening.
And he who eats from its carcass shall wash his garments, and be impure until the evening; and he who carries its carcass shall wash his garments, and be impure until the evening.
And every swarming creature that swarms upon the earth, a detestable thing it is; it shall not be eaten.

All that walks upon the belly, and all that walks upon four, up to all that has many feet, for all the swarming creatures that swarm upon the earth, you shall not eat them, for a detestable thing they are.
You shall not make detestable your souls with any swarming creature that swarms, and you shall not be impure by them, and you shall become impure by them.
For I am Havayah your Elokim, and you shall sanctify yourselves, and be holy, for I am holy, and you shall not make impure your souls with any swarming creature that creeps upon the earth.
For I am Havayah, who brings you up from the land of Mitzrayim, to be for you an Elokim, and you shall be holy, for I am holy.
This is the law of the animal, and of the bird, and of every living soul that creeps in the water, and of every soul that swarms upon the earth.
To distinguish between the impure and between the pure, and between the living creature that is eaten and between the living creature that is not eaten.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, saying: A woman when she conceives, and bears a male, and she shall be impure seven days, like the days of the separation of her suffering she shall be impure.
And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
And thirty days and three days she shall dwell in the blood of purity; any sacred thing she shall not touch, and to the Sanctuary she shall not come, until the completion of the days of her purity.
And if a female she bears, and she shall be impure two weeks, as her separation, and sixty days and six days she shall dwell in the blood of purity.

And when the days of her purity are complete, for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring a year-old lamb for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest.
And he shall bring it near before Havayah, and atone for her, and she shall be purified from the source of her blood; this is the law of the woman who gives birth, to a male or to a female.

And if her hand does not find enough for a lamb, and she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering, and the priest shall atone for her, and she shall be purified.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:

A man, when there is in the skin of his flesh a rising, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his flesh a mark of tzaraas, and he shall be brought to Aharon the priest, or to one of his sons, the priests.

And the priest shall see the mark in the skin of the flesh, and hair in the mark turned white, and the appearance of the mark is deeper than the skin of his flesh, a mark of tzaraas it is, and the priest shall see it, and declare it impure.
And if a white bright spot is in the skin of his flesh, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, and the priest shall shut up the mark seven days.
And the priest shall see it on the seventh day, and behold, the mark stood in his eyes, the mark has not spread in the skin, and the priest shall shut him up seven days a second time.

And the priest shall see it on the seventh day a second time, and behold, the mark has faded, and the mark has not spread in the skin, and the priest shall declare him pure; a scab it is, and he shall wash his garments, and be pure.
And if the scab spreads in the skin, after he was shown to the priest for his purification, and he shall be shown a second time to the priest.
And the priest shall see, and behold, the scab has spread in the skin, and the priest shall declare him impure; tzaraas it is.
A mark of tzaraas, when it is on a man, and he shall be brought to the priest.
And the priest shall see, and behold, a white rising in the skin, and it has turned hair white, and a growth of live flesh in the rising.
It is old tzaraas in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall declare him impure; he shall not shut him up, for impure he is.
And if the tzaraas breaks out in the skin, and covers the tzaraas all the skin of the mark, from his head to his feet, for all the sight of the eyes of the priest.
And the priest shall see, and behold, the tzaraas has covered all his flesh, and he shall declare the mark pure; all of it has turned white, pure he is.
And on the day there is seen in him live flesh, he shall be impure.
And the priest shall see the live flesh, and declare him impure; the live flesh, impure it is, tzaraas it is.
Or when returns the live flesh and turns white, and he shall come to the priest.
And the priest shall see him, and behold, the mark has turned white, and the priest shall declare the mark pure; pure he is.
And flesh, when there is in it in its skin a rash, and it is healed.
And there is in the place of the rash a white rising, or a white-reddish bright spot, and it shall be shown to the priest.
And the priest shall see, and behold, its appearance is lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, and the priest shall declare him impure; a mark of tzaraas it is, in the rash it broke out.
And if the priest sees it, and behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, and the priest shall shut him up seven days.
And if it spreads in the skin, and the priest shall declare him impure; a mark it is.
And if in its place stands the bright spot, it has not spread, a scar of the rash it is, and the priest shall declare him pure.
Or flesh, when there is in its skin a burn of fire, and there is the healing of the burn, a white-reddish or white bright spot.

And the priest shall see it, and behold, hair has turned white in the bright spot, and its appearance is deeper than the skin, tzaraas it is, in the burn it broke out, and the priest shall declare him impure; a mark of tzaraas it is.
And if the priest sees it, and behold, there is no white hair in the bright spot, and it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, and the priest shall shut him up seven days.
And the priest shall see him on the seventh day, if it spreads in the skin, and the priest shall declare him impure; a mark of tzaraas it is.
And if in its place stands the bright spot, it has not spread in the skin, and it is faded, a rising of the burn it is, and the priest shall declare him pure, for a scar of the burn it is.
And a man or a woman, when there is in him a mark, in the head or in the beard.

And the priest shall see the mark, and behold, its appearance is deeper than the skin, and in it is yellow, thin hair, and the priest shall declare him impure; a scall it is, tzaraas of the head or of the beard it is.

And when the priest sees the mark of the scall, and behold, its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and black hair there is none in it, and the priest shall shut up the mark of the scall seven days.
And the priest shall see the mark on the seventh day, and behold, the scall has not spread, and there was no yellow hair in it, and the appearance of the scall is not deeper than the skin.
And he shall shave himself, and the scall he shall not shave, and the priest shall shut up the scall seven days a second time.

And the priest shall see the scall on the seventh day, and behold, the scall has not spread in the skin, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and the priest shall declare him pure, and he shall wash his garments, and be pure.
And if the scall spreads in the skin after his purification.
And the priest shall see him, and behold, the scall has spread in the skin, the priest shall not look for the yellow hair; impure he is.
And if in his eyes the scall has stood, and black hair has grown in it, the scall is healed, pure he is, and the priest shall declare him pure.
And a man or a woman, when there is in the skin of their flesh white bright spots.
And the priest shall see, and behold, in the skin of their flesh faded, white bright spots, a tetter it is, it broke out in the skin; pure he is.
And a man, when the hair of his head falls out, bald he is; pure he is.
And if from the side of his face the hair of his head falls out, frontally bald he is; pure he is.
And when there is on the bald head or on the bald forehead a mark, white-reddish, it is tzaraas breaking out, on his bald head or on his bald forehead.
And the priest shall see it, and behold, the rising of the mark is white-reddish on his bald head or on his bald forehead, like the appearance of tzaraas of the skin of the flesh.
A man of tzaraas he is, impure he is; the priest shall declare him impure, declaring impure, on his head is his mark.
And the metzora in whom the mark is, his garments shall be torn, and his head shall be left wild, and upon his lip he shall cover, and: Impure, impure, he shall call.
All the days that the mark is in him he shall be impure; impure he is; alone he shall dwell, outside the camp shall be his dwelling.
And the garment, when there is in it a mark of tzaraas, in a garment of wool or in a garment of linen.
Or in warp or in woof, for the linen and for the wool, or in leather, or in any work of leather.
And the mark is greenish or reddish, in the garment or in the leather, or in the warp or in the woof, or in any leather vessel, a mark of tzaraas it is, and it shall be shown to the priest.
And the priest shall see the mark, and shall shut up the mark seven days.

And the priest shall see the mark on the seventh day, for the mark has spread in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in the leather, for all that the leather is made for work, the mark is malignant tzaraas, impure it is.
And he shall burn the garment, or the warp, or the woof, in the wool or in the linen, or any leather vessel in which there is the mark, for it is malignant tzaraas; in fire it shall be burned.
And if the priest sees, and behold, the mark has not spread in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather vessel.
And the priest shall command, and they shall wash that in which the mark is, and shall shut it up seven days a second time.

And the priest shall see after the mark has been washed, and behold, the mark has not changed its appearance, and the mark has not spread, impure it is; in fire you shall burn it, a hollow it is, on its bald back or on its bald front.
And if the priest sees, and behold, the mark has faded after it has been washed, and he shall tear it from the garment, or from the leather, or from the warp, or from the woof.
And if it is seen again in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any leather vessel, breaking out it is; in fire you shall burn it, that in which the mark is.
And the garment, or the warp, or the woof, or any leather vessel, that you shall wash, and the mark departs from them, and it shall be washed a second time, and it shall be pure.
This is the law of the mark of tzaraas of a garment of wool or of linen, or of the warp or of the woof, or of any leather vessel, to declare it pure or to declare it impure.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
This shall be the law of the metzora on the day of his purification, and he shall be brought to the priest.
And the priest shall go out to outside the camp, and the priest shall see, and behold, the mark of tzaraas has been healed from the metzora.
And the priest shall command, and shall take for the one being purified two living birds, pure, and cedar wood, and scarlet wool, and hyssop.
And the priest shall command, and he shall slaughter the one bird, in an earthenware vessel, over living water.
The living bird he shall take, and the cedar wood, and the scarlet wool, and the hyssop, and dip them and the living bird in the blood of the slaughtered bird, over the living water.
And he shall sprinkle upon the one being purified from the tzaraas seven times, and declare him pure, and send away the living bird upon the face of the field.
And the one being purified shall wash his garments, and shave all his hair, and bathe in water, and be pure, and afterward he shall come to the camp, and dwell outside his tent seven days.

And it shall be on the seventh day, he shall shave all his hair, his head and his beard and the brows of his eyes, and all his hair he shall shave, and wash his garments, and bathe his flesh in water, and be pure.
And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished lambs, and one unblemished year-old ewe, and three-tenths of fine flour, a meal offering mixed with oil, and one log of oil.
And the priest who purifies shall set the man who is being purified, and them, before Havayah, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And the priest shall take the one lamb, and present it as a guilt offering, and the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before Havayah.

And he shall slaughter the lamb in the place where he slaughters the sin offering and the burnt offering, in the holy place, for as the sin offering the guilt offering is for the priest; a holy of holies it is.

And the priest shall take from the blood of the guilt offering, and the priest shall put upon the tip of the right ear of the one being purified, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot.
And the priest shall take from the log of oil, and pour it upon the left palm of the priest.
And the priest shall dip his right finger from the oil that is upon his left palm, and sprinkle from the oil with his finger seven times before Havayah.

And from the rest of the oil that is upon his palm, the priest shall put upon the tip of the right ear of the one being purified, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the guilt offering.
And the remainder of the oil that is upon the palm of the priest he shall put upon the head of the one being purified, and the priest shall atone for him before Havayah.
And the priest shall do the sin offering, and atone for the one being purified from his impurity, and afterward he shall slaughter the burnt offering.
And the priest shall bring up the burnt offering and the meal offering upon the altar, and the priest shall atone for him, and he shall be pure.

And if he is poor, and his hand does not reach, and he shall take one lamb, a guilt offering for waving, to atone for him, and one-tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil.
And two turtledoves or two young pigeons, that his hand reaches, and one shall be a sin offering and the one a burnt offering.
And he shall bring them on the eighth day of his purification to the priest, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, before Havayah.
And the priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them as a wave offering before Havayah.

And he shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest shall take from the blood of the guilt offering, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of the one being purified, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot.
And from the oil the priest shall pour upon the left palm of the priest.
And the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger from the oil that is upon his left palm seven times before Havayah.

And the priest shall put from the oil that is upon his palm upon the tip of the right ear of the one being purified, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the big toe of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
And the remainder of the oil that is upon the palm of the priest he shall put upon the head of the one being purified, to atone for him before Havayah.
And he shall do the one from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons, from that which his hand reaches.
That which his hand reaches, the one a sin offering and the one a burnt offering, upon the meal offering, and the priest shall atone for the one being purified before Havayah.
This is the law of one in whom there is a mark of tzaraas, whose hand does not reach in his purification.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:
When you come to the land of Kena'an, which I give to you as a portion, and I place a mark of tzaraas in a house of the land of your portion.
And he to whom the house belongs shall come, and tell the priest, saying: Like a mark it seems to me in the house.

And the priest shall command, and they shall empty the house, before the priest comes to see the mark, and all that is in the house shall not become impure, and afterward the priest shall come to see the house.
And the priest shall see the mark, and behold, the mark is in the walls of the house, hollowed, greenish or reddish, and their appearance is lower than the wall.
And the priest shall go out from the house to the entrance of the house, and shall shut up the house seven days.
And the priest shall return on the seventh day, and see, and behold, the mark has spread in the walls of the house.
And the priest shall command, and they shall pull out the stones on which the mark is, and throw them to outside the city, to an impure place.
And the house he shall scrape inside, all around, and they shall pour out the plaster that they scraped, to outside the city, to an impure place.
And they shall take other stones, and bring them in place of the stones, and other plaster he shall take, and plaster the house.
And if returns the mark and breaks out in the house, after he pulled out the stones, and after he scraped the house, and after it was plastered.
And the priest shall come and see, and behold, the mark has spread in the house, tzaraas malignant it is in the house, impure it is.
And he shall tear down the house, its stones, and its timbers, and all the plaster of the house, and take it out to outside the city, to an impure place.
And he who comes to the house all the days that it is shut up shall be impure until the evening.
And he who lies in the house shall wash his garments, and he who eats in the house shall wash his garments.
And if the priest comes and sees, and behold, the mark has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, and the priest shall declare the house pure, for the mark was healed.
And he shall take, to cleanse the house, two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet wool, and hyssop.
And he shall slaughter the one bird, in an earthenware vessel, over living water.

And he shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet wool, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the living water, and sprinkle upon the house seven times.
And he shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, and with the living water, and with the living bird, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet wool.
And he shall send away the living bird to outside the city, upon the face of the field, and atone for the house, and it shall be pure.
This is the law for every mark of tzaraas, and for the scall.
And for tzaraas of the garment, and of the house.
And for the rising, and for the scab, and for the bright spot.
To teach on the day of the impure and on the day of the pure; this is the law of tzaraas.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, and say to them: A man, a man, when he is a zav from his flesh, his discharge, impure it is.
And this shall be his impurity in his discharge: his flesh runs with his discharge, or his flesh is stopped up from his discharge, his impurity it is.
Every bed on which the zav lies upon it shall be impure, and every vessel on which he sits upon it shall be impure.
And a man who touches his bedding shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And he who sits upon the vessel on which the zav sat upon it shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And he who touches the flesh of the zav shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And when the zav spits upon the pure, and he shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And every saddle on which the zav rides upon it shall be impure.
And all who touch anything that is under him shall be impure until the evening, and he who carries them shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And all that the zav touches, and his hands he has not rinsed in water, and he shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And an earthenware vessel that the zav touches shall be broken, and every wooden vessel shall be rinsed in water.
And when the zav is cleansed from his discharge, and he shall count for himself seven days for his purification, and wash his garments, and bathe his flesh in living water, and be pure.
And on the eighth day he shall take for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and come before Havayah to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
And the priest shall do them, one a sin offering and one a burnt offering, and the priest shall atone for him before Havayah from his discharge.
And a man, when a lying of seed goes out from him, and he shall bathe in water all his flesh, and be impure until the evening.
And every garment and every leather upon which there is a lying of seed, and it shall be washed in water, and be impure until the evening.
And a woman with whom a man lies, a lying of seed, and they shall bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And a woman, when she is a zavah, her discharge shall be blood in her flesh; seven days she shall be in her niddah, and all who touch her shall be impure until the evening.
And all that she lies upon in her niddah shall be impure, and all that she sits upon shall be impure.
And all who touch her bedding shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And all who touch any vessel on which she sits upon it shall wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And if upon the bed it is, or upon the vessel on which she sits upon it, in his touching it, he shall be impure until the evening.
And if a man lies with her, and her niddah is upon him, and he shall be impure seven days, and every bed on which he lies upon it shall be impure.

And a woman, when the discharge of her blood flows many days, not at the time of her niddah, or when she flows beyond her niddah, all the days of the discharge of her impurity, as the days of her niddah she shall be, impure she is.

Every bed on which she lies upon it all the days of her discharge, as the bed of her niddah it shall be for her, and every vessel on which she sits upon it shall be impure, as the impurity of her niddah.
And all who touch them shall be impure, and wash his garments, and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening.
And if she is cleansed from her discharge, and she shall count for herself seven days, and afterward she shall be pure.
And on the eighth day she shall take for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and bring them to the priest, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And the priest shall do the one a sin offering and the one a burnt offering, and the priest shall atone for her before Havayah from the discharge of her impurity.
And you shall set apart the children of Yisroel from their impurity, and they shall not die in their impurity, in their making impure My Mishkan that is in their midst.
This is the law of the zav, and of one from whom a lying of seed goes out, to become impure by it.
And she who suffers in her niddah, and the zav with his discharge, for the male and for the female, and for a man who lies with an impure woman.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe after the death of the two sons of Aharon, in their coming near before Havayah, and they died.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Speak to Aharon your brother, and let him not come at all times into the Sanctum, from within the curtain, before the cover that is upon the ark, and let him not die, for in the cloud I shall be seen upon the cover.
With this Aharon shall come into the Sanctum: with a bull, a young of the cattle, for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

He shall wear a sacred linen tunic, and trousers of linen shall be upon his flesh, and with a belt of linen he shall gird himself, and with a mitre of linen he shall wrap himself; sacred garments they are, and he shall bathe in water his flesh, and wear them.
And from the congregation of the children of Yisroel he shall take two goats, for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.
And Aharon shall present the bull of the sin offering that is for him, and shall atone for himself and for his household.
And he shall take the two goats, and set them before Havayah, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And Aharon shall give lots upon the two goats, one lot for Havayah, and one lot for Azazel.
And Aharon shall present the goat on which the lot for Havayah came up, and shall make it a sin offering.
And the goat on which the lot for Azazel came up shall be set alive before Havayah, to atone upon it, to dispatch it to Azazel, to the wilderness.
And Aharon shall present the bull of the sin offering that is for him, and shall atone for himself and for his household, and shall slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is for him.
And he shall take a fire-pan full of coals of fire from upon the altar from before Havayah, and the fullness of his hands of incense of spices, finely ground, and bring within the curtain.
And he shall put the incense upon the fire before Havayah, and the cloud of the incense shall cover the cover that is upon the testimony, and he shall not die.
And he shall take from the blood of the bull, and sprinkle with his finger upon the face of the cover, eastward, and before the cover he shall sprinkle seven times from the blood with his finger.

And he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people, and bring its blood within the curtain, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it upon the cover and before the cover.

And he shall atone for the Sanctum from the impurity of the children of Yisroel, and from their transgressions, for all their sins, and so he shall do for the Tent of Meeting, that dwells with them in the midst of their impurity.
And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he comes to atone in the Sanctum until his going out, and he shall atone for himself and for his household and for all the assembly of Yisroel.
And he shall go out to the altar that is before Havayah, and atone upon it, and take from the blood of the bull and from the blood of the goat, and put upon the horns of the altar all around.
And he shall sprinkle upon it from the blood with his finger seven times, and purify it and sanctify it from the impurity of the children of Yisroel.
And he shall finish atoning for the Sanctum and for the Tent of Meeting and for the altar, and he shall present the living goat.

And Aharon shall lay his two hands upon the head of the living goat, and confess upon it all the iniquities of the children of Yisroel, and all their transgressions, for all their sins, and put them upon the head of the goat, and dispatch it by the hand of a designated man to the wilderness.
And the goat shall bear upon it all their iniquities to a land cut off, and he shall dispatch the goat in the wilderness.
And Aharon shall come into the Tent of Meeting, and strip off the linen garments that he wore when he came into the Sanctum, and leave them there.
And he shall bathe his flesh in water in a holy place, and wear his garments, and go out and do his burnt offering and the burnt offering of the people, and atone for himself and for the people.
And the fat of the sin offering he shall burn upon the altar.
And he who dispatches the goat to Azazel shall wash his garments and bathe his flesh in water, and after that he shall come into the camp.

And the bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought to atone in the Sanctum, he shall take them outside the camp, and they shall burn in fire their hides and their flesh and their dung.
And he who burns them shall wash his garments and bathe his flesh in water, and after that he shall come into the camp.

And it shall be for you an eternal statute: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and all work you shall not do, the native and the stranger who sojourns among you.
For on this day he shall atone for you, to purify you; from all your sins before Havayah you shall be purified.
A sabbath of rest it is for you, and you shall afflict your souls; an eternal statute.
And the priest who shall be anointed, and who shall fill his hand to serve as priest in place of his father, shall atone, and he shall wear the linen garments, the sacred garments.
And he shall atone for the Holy of Holies, and for the Tent of Meeting and for the altar he shall atone, and for the priests and for all the people of the assembly he shall atone.
And this shall be for you an eternal statute, to atone for the children of Yisroel from all their sins once in the year; and he did as Havayah commanded Moshe.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to Aharon and to his sons and to all the children of Yisroel, and say to them: This is the matter that Havayah has commanded, saying:
A man, a man from the house of Yisroel who slaughters a bull or a sheep or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters outside the camp.

And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it, to present an offering to Havayah before the Mishkan of Havayah, blood shall be reckoned for that man; he has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people.

So that the children of Yisroel shall bring their slaughtered animals that they slaughter upon the face of the field, and bring them to Havayah, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and slaughter them as peace offerings to Havayah.
And the priest shall cast the blood upon the altar of Havayah, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and burn the fat for a pleasing aroma to Havayah.
And they shall no longer slaughter their slaughterings to the satyrs, after whom they go astray; an eternal statute shall this be for them, for their generations.
And to them you shall say: A man, a man from the house of Yisroel, and from the stranger who sojourns among them, who offers up a burnt offering or a slaughtering.
And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he does not bring it, to do it to Havayah, and that man shall be cut off from his people.

And a man, a man from the house of Yisroel, and from the stranger who sojourns among them, who eats any blood, and I shall set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and cut it off from the midst of its people.
For the soul of the flesh, in the blood it is, and I have given it to you upon the altar, to atone for your souls, for it is the blood that atones, by the soul.
Therefore I said to the children of Yisroel: Every soul among you shall not eat blood, and the stranger who sojourns among you shall not eat blood.

And a man, a man from the children of Yisroel, and from the stranger who sojourns among them, who hunts game, a beast or a bird that may be eaten, and he shall pour out its blood, and cover it with dust.

For the soul of all flesh, its blood, with its soul it is, and I said to the children of Yisroel: The blood of all flesh you shall not eat, for the soul of all flesh, it is its blood; all who eat it shall be cut off.
And every soul that eats a carcass or a torn animal, whether native or stranger, and he shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be impure until the evening, and be purified.
And if he does not wash, and his flesh he does not bathe, and he shall bear his iniquity.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the children of Yisroel, and say to them: I am Havayah your Elokim.

Like the practice of the land of Mitzrayim, in which you dwelled, you shall not do, and like the practice of the land of Kena'an, which I am bringing you there, you shall not do, and in their statutes you shall not walk.
My ordinances you shall do, and My statutes you shall keep, to walk in them; I am Havayah your Elokim.
And you shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, which a man shall do them and live by them; I am Havayah.
A man, a man, to any kin of his flesh you shall not approach to uncover nakedness; I am Havayah.
The nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover; your mother she is, you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover; your father's nakedness it is.
The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, born in the house or born outside, you shall not uncover their nakedness.
The nakedness of the daughter of your son or the daughter of your daughter you shall not uncover their nakedness, for your nakedness they are.
The nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father, your sister she is, you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your father's sister you shall not uncover; the kin of your father she is.
The nakedness of your mother's sister you shall not uncover, for the kin of your mother she is.
The nakedness of your father's brother you shall not uncover; to his wife you shall not approach; your aunt she is.
The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover; your son's wife she is, you shall not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover; your brother's nakedness it is.

The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover; the daughter of her son and the daughter of her daughter you shall not take to uncover her nakedness; her kin they are, lewdness it is.
And a woman with her sister you shall not take, to make rivals, to uncover her nakedness upon her in her lifetime.
And to a woman in the impurity of her niddah you shall not approach to uncover her nakedness.
And to the wife of your fellow you shall not give your lying of seed, to defile yourself with her.
And from your seed you shall not give to pass to Molekh, and you shall not profane the name of your Elokim; I am Havayah.
And with a male you shall not lie as one lies with a woman; an abomination it is.
And with any beast you shall not give your lying, to defile yourself with it, and a woman shall not stand before a beast to mate with it; a perversion it is.
Do not defile yourselves in all these, for in all these were defiled the nations that I am sending forth from before you.
And the land was defiled, and I visited its iniquity upon it, and the land spewed out its inhabitants.
And you shall keep My statutes and My ordinances, and you shall not do any of these abominations, the native and the stranger who sojourns among you.
For the men of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land was defiled.
And the land shall not spew you out by your defiling it, as it spewed out the nation that was before you.
For all who do any of these abominations, the souls that do shall be cut off from among their people.
And you shall keep My charge, not to do any of the abominable statutes that were done before you, and you shall not defile yourselves by them; I am Havayah your Elokim.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to all the congregation of the children of Yisroel, and say to them: Holy you shall be, for I am holy, Havayah your Elokim.
A man, his mother and his father, you shall fear, and My Shabbosos you shall keep; I am Havayah your Elokim.
Do not turn to the elilim, and you shall not make gods of molten metal for yourselves; I am Havayah your Elokim.
And when you slaughter a slaughtering of peace offerings to Havayah, for your acceptance you shall slaughter it.
On the day of your slaughtering it shall be eaten, and on the morrow, and what remains until the third day, in fire it shall be burned.
And if eating it is eaten on the third day, piggul it is, it shall not be accepted.
And those who eat it shall bear their iniquity, for the sacred of Havayah he has profaned, and that soul shall be cut off from its people.
And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the corner of your field to reap, and the gleanings of your harvest you shall not gather.
And your vineyard you shall not glean, and the fallen fruit of your vineyard you shall not gather; for the poor and for the stranger you shall leave them; I am Havayah your Elokim.
You shall not steal, and you shall not deny, and you shall not lie, a man to his fellow.
And you shall not swear by My name falsely, and you shall profane the name of your Elokim; I am Havayah.
You shall not oppress your neighbor, and you shall not rob; the wages of a hired laborer shall not remain with you until morning.
You shall not curse a deaf man, and before a blind man you shall not put a stumbling block, and you shall fear your Elokim; I am Havayah.
You shall not do injustice in judgment; you shall not favor the face of the poor, and you shall not honor the face of the great; with righteousness you shall judge your fellow.
You shall not go as a talebearer among your people; you shall not stand by the blood of your neighbor; I am Havayah.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your fellow, and you shall not bear a sin because of him.
You shall not take vengeance, and you shall not bear a grudge against the children of your people, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am Havayah.
My statutes you shall keep; your beast you shall not mate with diverse kinds; your field you shall not sow with diverse kinds; and a garment of mixed kinds, sha'atnez, shall not come upon you.

And a man, when he lies with a woman, a lying of seed, and she is a maidservant designated for a man, and she was not redeemed, or freedom was not given to her, there shall be an inspection; they shall not be put to death, for she was not freed.
And he shall bring his guilt offering to Havayah, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a ram of a guilt offering.
And the priest shall atone for him with the ram of the guilt offering before Havayah, for his sin that he sinned, and it shall be forgiven to him for his sin that he sinned.
